content:
We now have a radar instance at https://radar.lean-lang.org/repos/tauceti that tracks performance metrics for the build, and provides graphs showing e.g. total instruction count over time.

(Obviously the time series is not very extensive yet, it just contains the last 10 or so commits so far.)

Hopefully this will be useful diagnosing the inevitable PRs that do something terrible to compile time!

You can now run !bench on PRs to get a report. The "signficance" filtering isn't live yet, but Joscha tells me this will happen automatically as radar gathers data.

I think for now let's not wire this into the automatic review process, but it is a possibility for the future.

Hi, @Kim Morrison , may I ask to add Lean Pool to the radar? It looks like a very useful tool!
Totally understand if it's not possible since it's not an "official" LeanFRO/MI repo, but I figured it's worth asking :)
Sorry, I think I can't promise that as yet, I'm taking advantage of some insider access there. What I can do is investigate how hard it is to set up a radar runner externally.

Are there rules on build time for PRs? I think it could be good to have a policy of replacing existing code with whatever builds the fastest and proves the same theorems, but probably with some safeguards so that everyone doesn't start minifying their code to make it build faster.

The main rule so far is that there are no set_option in Tau Ceti, particularly no set_option maxHeartbeats, and this in practice prevents many of the build time problems.

(This is apparently not enforced in CI yet, I'll go add that now!)

I'm hesitant to have a "build time monotonicity" rule for refactors. Maybe a "Don't increase build time by 2x"? If anyone would like to add infrastructure so that radar reports get posted in a topic here, that would be wonderful.
You can borrow Lean Pool's profiling methodology. I found it very useful.

Kim Morrison said:

(This is apparently not enforced in CI yet, I'll go add that now!)

Done in TauCeti#1034.

Vasily Ilin said:

You can borrow Lean Pool's profiling methodology. I found it very useful.

TauCeti#1035 adds a CI step that posts advisory comments on PRs that (approximately, this isn't perfect) increase the heartbeat count of an existing file by more than 1.5x.
Why not just use the same system as mathlib and FLT and have that radar bot pointing out when a commit contributes a major change?

radar is only after the fact, whereas this mechanism posts on PRs as they are created.

(Note that we do have radar for Tau Ceti, https://radar.lean-lang.org/repos/tauceti, but we haven't yet hooked it up to post regularly to Zulip. I'll try to do that shortly.
